required_changes: Limit the print punctuation cleanup to the spaces that removed conditionals leave behind. close_up_whitespace (compiler.py:1459-1482) now calls close_before_punctuation on every text and tail under every tei:p and tei:l. That includes notes and rubrics, and it runs for both print and electronic compiles. Any space before , . ; : ! ? or ׃ in the source text is deleted, in every language except French. Two examples: spaced ellipses ('and . . . then' becomes 'and... then'), and older English or documentary editions that print 'Lord ;' or 'thee ?'. The PR says it changes no source-book words, but this changes how unrelated source text is laid out. The cleanest fix is to close the space only where a dropped conditional's text is joined to the text before it, in CompilerProcessor._carry_dropped_tail (compiler.py:862-884). That is the only place that knows the join came from a removed scope. If the global pass stays, do two things: (a) never collapse a space before '.' when the next character is '.', so ellipses survive; (b) run a before/after diff of compiled text across the whole corpus and show that every change is at a removed-conditional junction.

Add an automated check, a test or a recorded headless-browser assertion, that the visible text reads 'word insert:' with the space when the scope is true and when it is undecided/undefined. The separator space is now an untyped tei:seg inside its own silent scope. html.xslt uses on-no-match="shallow-skip" (html.xslt:61), and I could not confirm which template handles an untyped tei:seg or a whitespace-only text node inside one. The existing browser JSON only records spaceBeforeGoyimColon=false for all four cases. That shows the space is hidden when false. It does not show the space survives when true. No case explicitly covers the undefined state, where a silent scope and a marked scope with the same predicate must both show. If the space is lost, true/undefined output becomes 'wordinsert:', which is exactly what the PR says cannot happen.
additional_checks:
Newline before the colon, in both print and HTML. If the source has a line break plus indentation between the word and the conditional ('word
      <j:conditional/>…<j:endConditional/>:'), close_up_whitespace produces 'word
:' because its patterns only match [ 	]. _conditional_separators matches r'[ 	]+$' and leaves the '
' in place. In both TeX and HTML that newline still shows as a space before the colon. Check whether any real inserts are encoded across lines. If so, include newlines before closing punctuation (the importer only adds newlines after punctuation).

Lines holding only marker leaves (reledmac.xslt:3402-3405). Any tei:l where f:sets-text is false, with no lb/space/gap/graphic/page ref and no p:part='last', now gets no lb. Confirm that's acceptable for: (a) an l holding only the closer of an undecided marked scope (its ']' would now start the next verse instead of ending the line before); (b) an l holding only an opener whose bracket or rule would now run into the next line; (c) an l holding only an editorial note or its anchor. Add synthetic tests for an l with only a rubric (break must stay, through the descendant-or-self rubric branch) and one with only an undecided marked opener or closer.

Confirm f:sets-text's list of text-bearing leaves (text, hi, c, emph, foreign, choice, ref, rubric, f:head, f:list-label) covers every element the leaves mode keeps whole rather than descending into. Pay particular attention to anything this inline-divine-name branch emits as a whole leaf. A line made up only of such an element would lose its break.

A whole verse removed across a parallel boundary: if both p:part='first' and p:part='last' fragments are left with only markers, the 'last' fragment still emits an lb, so a blank row remains. Check whether this happens in the Mahzor and parallel books.
Parallel output: check that suppressing the lb for empty l elements in one column doesn't break row or pstart pairing, or the trimming done by f:trim-trailing-breaks, against the other column.

Check the HTML separator scope's side effects: Feature.cids and Feature.scopes go up by one per separator (markers.py:182-186), while chars, sections and rows are unaffected because the run is whitespace only. Make sure the settings panel or ranking doesn't show inflated passage counts.

Performance: f:sets-text re-runs the leaves mode over every non-fragment tei:l. Swap the order so the cheap exists(.//tei:lb | …) test runs before f:sets-text, and spot-check transform time on a long poetry book (e.g. Tehillim).
limitations: This review covered the cited ranges of reledmac.xslt, whitespace.py, close_up_whitespace in compiler.py, markers.py (all of it), conditional_markers.py, the new test file, the logs, and the browser-check JSON. I only had file reads: no grep, and I ran nothing. I did not trace how j:conditional and j:endConditional are emitted in leaves/emit mode, the html.xslt templates for tei:seg and text(), or the reader-device JS that decides how silent and marked scopes are shown when undefined.

I did not look at the before-fix screenshots or the PDFs being rendered separately. The test logs show only pass counts (516/730, 167/55, 184/186) without test names, so I can't tell from them which tests cover the changed code.

_conditional_separators only handles an opener and closer with the same parent inside a tei:p or tei:l, with the punctuation at the very start of the closer's tail. Punctuation after an intervening element (a note anchor, an enclosing closer), or inserts inside tei:head, tei:ab or tei:item, are not handled. These are coverage gaps, not regressions.
notes: The XSLT change does what was described. Marker leaves are still emitted, because node() is always processed in leaves mode; only the l's own trailing lb depends on the new condition. first/middle fragments are unchanged, p:part='last' still closes its line, and an explicit lb, space, gap, graphic or page ref keeps the break. The four TeX tests cover the stanza-milestone, page-label, final-fragment and explicit-lb cases.

The HTML separator scope is built correctly as far as I can see. The deepcopy keeps the condition and p:pinned, so _number_scopes gives it the same expression index (the test asserts this). It drops @type, p:silent and every tei:note child. Its tail is None and the next node is a tei:seg rather than a rubric note, so mark_silent_scopes classes it as silent. The new id is unique. The space sits before the original marked opener, so the brackets and their text are unchanged. _assign labels the seg because it is an element; whitespace-only text runs are deliberately not wrapped.

The French rule in closing_punctuation (only ,.׃ for fr*) and keeping NBSP both behave as stated; NBSP, U+202F and U+2009 never match [ \t]. Language comes from the parent for tails and from the element for text, which is correct.
Undecided scopes in print aren't affected by close_up_whitespace, because its substitutions never cross element boundaries. 'word [insert]:' keeps its spacing.

Smaller points: earlier_text in _conditional_separators includes the text of earlier notes and rubrics, so an insert at the start of a paragraph after a rubric still gets a separator scope (harmless). Tests that count r'\leavevmode\\{}' are fragile; asserting the exact sequence of leaves would be sturdier.
No source readings were reopened. The first required change is about the exporter applying the cleanup globally, not about any adjudicated text.
